source.title: Optimum release time for software systems based on reliability and cost criteria

confidence_rationale: Foundational, heavily-cited peer-reviewed paper (high source_quality), but the mapping to Q-087 is by structural analogy rather than direct application: it optimises a continuous timing decision for a single software product under a quantifiable reliability/cost criterion, whereas Q-087 concerns a discrete, deliberately NON-metric governance milestone across a heterogeneous research substrate. It grounds the resolution's core reasoning (readiness is a chosen criterion applied under uncertainty, not the passive attainment of a defect-free state) but cannot itself adjudicate a governance judgement call, so confidence is held to moderate and mapping_fidelity is weighted heavily.
failure_signatures: The model presupposes a quantifiable software-reliability metric and a cost function; a governance-acceptance criterion is explicitly non-metric, so the paper's optimisation machinery does not transfer, only its framing that release is a decision against a criterion.

It optimises WHEN to release a converging reliability curve, not WHAT event constitutes closure of a system with permanently-blocked components -- the 'may never converge' case Q-087's strict-green-board candidate faced is outside the model's assumptions.

mapping.source_claim_statement: The paper addresses 'the problem of determining the optimum time when testing can stop and a system can be considered ready for operational use,' which 'depends on both the model for the software failure phenomenon and the criterion used for evaluating system readiness'; two criteria are investigated -- software reliability and total expected cost -- and 'based on the cost criterion, an optimum release policy is derived.'
mapping.ree_translation: Declaring a software version 'ready' (closed) is a decision derived from an explicitly-chosen readiness criterion under uncertainty, not the emergent arrival of a defect-free or all-green state. This supports Q-087's resolution that V3 closure be a governance decision recorded against a criterion (governance_acceptance), and specifically supports the resolution's rejection of the strict-green-board candidate on the grounds that an exhaustive-completeness event 'may never fire.'
mapping.mapping_caveat: The transfer is analogical. Okumoto-Goel still assumes a measurable reliability metric that monotonically improves and a cost model to trade against it; Q-087 deliberately chose a non-metric governance event precisely because the metric (green-board node count) may never reach completion. The paper concerns a deployed software product's operational readiness, not the freezing of a research substrate as a causal reference artefact.
mapping.source_context: Software reliability engineering; analytical optimisation of software release timing for a single product using the Goel-Okumoto NHPP failure model.

confidence_components.notes: High source quality (canonical, peer-reviewed, decades of citation). Mapping fidelity moderate: the paper's decision-theoretic framing maps well, but its metric/cost apparatus does not transfer to a non-metric governance event. Transfer risk moderate-to-high: software-product-timing -> governance-milestone-definition is a domain jump. Aggregate weighted toward mapping_fidelity as an architectural/governance claim.
